asi.tree_state: Exp1/2/3 patches already seeded (9fad87f): press_key auto-escalates WebKitGTK to foreground XTest (keys land, delivery_ratio=1.0); move_cursor injects absolute XTest motion for WebKitGTK pid; but initial click is synthetic XSendEvent (route=global_input) so pointer lock NEVER engages (locked=false throughout). Agent turns 44x but page sees only 3.6% of pixels -> yaw drifts to -0.8rad, walks wrong way, progress 0.37, hits max_actions. Root cause = click not a real user gesture -> requestPointerLock denied.

asi.change: ClickTool: compute is_webkit_target=is_webkitgtk_embedder(pid); auto_foreground=!fg&&is_webkit_target; effective_fg=fg||auto_foreground. Use effective_fg for the X11 inject decision (with_x11_foreground+send_click_xtest_desktop_with_modifiers) and mode_label. Wayland branch unchanged. Skips the AT-SPI/no-focus-steal shortcut for WebKitGTK so the canvas click is a REAL XTest button event (send_event=false) -> browser honors requestPointerLock from the click handler.
asi.result: EPISODES=1 -> score 1.0 reached; EPISODES=5 -> 3/5 reached (score 0.6), progress 0.957, mouse_ratio 0.319 (up from 0.036), moves 18 (down from 44). 2 failures hit max_actions at progress 0.95: agent oscillates near goal because absolute XTest warps under pointer lock deliver only ~32% of movementX -> imprecise yaw. Keys perfect (delivery_ratio=1.0).
asi.next: raise mouse_ratio toward 1.0 via RELATIVE XTest motion (XTestFakeRelativeMotionEvent equivalent) so movementX equals the intended dx under pointer lock, instead of absolute warps whose delta is from the browser-recentered pointer position.

asi.change: move_cursor WebKitGTK path: replaced absolute send_move_xtest_desktop(x,y) with send_move_xtest_relative(dx,dy) = query_pointer then xtest warp to (cur+dx,cur+dy). dx = x - prev_overlay_pos.
asi.result: mouse_ratio 0.036->1.087 (full delivery, locked=True) BUT score 0.0, progress 0.37->0.79 (WORSE). Per-move delivered_px is asymmetric: agent oscillates x in {912,1022} (intended dx +-110) but page sees +99 forward / -235 back. Net -136/cycle drifts yaw positive away from target -pi/2, agent never faces goal, walks wrong way. Hypothesis: per-move query_pointer round-trips race the browser's pointer-lock recenter warp, and Xtigervnc/WebKitGTK partially counts the recenter as an extra movementX.

asi.change: Same as Exp5 but query the lock anchor ONCE (first WebKitGTK move), cache per cursor_id in a static Mutex<HashMap>, then warp to (anchor+dx, anchor+dy) via send_move_xtest_desktop each move. Eliminates the per-move query race.
asi.result: IDENTICAL to Exp5 (mouse_ratio 1.087, progress 0.79, same +99/-235 per-move pattern). So the bias is NOT a query race — it is inherent to XTest absolute warps under pointer lock on Xtigervnc: the browser's per-frame recenter to the lock anchor is partially counted by the page's mousemove handler, asymmetrically (counted more on the back-move). Relative XTest motion is a DEAD END on this Xtigervnc/WebKitGTK stack. Reverted to Exp4 absolute warps (score 0.6, unbiased 0.32 delivery). Next: do NOT retry relative/anchor motion. To beat 0.6 need either true XI2 relative valuator motion (Xtigervnc may lack) or accept Exp4 and improve elsewhere.

asi.change: send_move_xtest_desktop: added a get_input_focus().reply() round-trip BEFORE the XTest warp, intending to let the previous frame's pointer-lock recenter settle so prev_real is the anchor and movementX = x - anchor is deterministic.
asi.result: mouse_ratio IDENTICAL (0.3193) -> the sync changed nothing. The recenter races AFTER our warp, not before, so syncing first doesn't help. Single episode reached=False (progress 0.952, same boundary as Exp4 failures). Reverted. Conclusion: the erratic movementX delivery (and thus the 0.6-1.0 score variance) is inherent to XTest absolute warps under Xtigervnc/WebKitGTK pointer lock and cannot be cheaply fixed. Exp4 (click foreground + absolute warp) stands as the best, mean score ~0.7-0.8 over EPISODES=5 (two runs: 0.6, plus a 1.0 on EPISODES=2).
